The order is sorted by billing month ascending, which means by the start date of the billing period.\n\nI'll sort by the billing period start date.\n\nNow for the implementation details:\n\n```python\nimport csv\nfrom datetime import datetime, timedelta\nimport calendar\nimport math\nfrom collections import defaultdict\nimport json\n\ndef answer() -> dict[str, list[int]]:\n    # Load employees\n    employees = {}\n    with open('/app/dataset/employees.csv', 'r') as f:\n        reader = csv.DictReader(f)\n        for row in reader:\n            pesel = row['PESEL'].strip()\n            hourly_rate = float(row['hourly_rate'].strip())\n            employees[pesel] = {'hourly_rate': hourly_rate}\n    \n    # Load tasks\n    tasks = {}\n    with open('/app/dataset/tasks.csv', 'r') as f:\n        reader = csv.DictReader(f)\n        for row in reader:\n            task_id = int(row['task_id'].strip())\n            pay = int(row['pay_per_completion'].strip())\n            tasks[task_id] = pay\n    \n    # Load timesheet\n    timesheet_entries = []\n    with open('/app/dataset/timesheet.csv', 'r') as f:\n        reader = csv.DictReader(f)\n        for row in reader:\n            entry = {\n                'id': int(row['id']),\n                'date_str': row['date'].strip(),\n                'hours_worked': float(row['hours_worked'].strip()),\n                'performed_tasks_str': row['performed_tasks'].strip(),\n                'employee_id': row['employee_id'].strip(),\n                'salary_amount': float(row['salary_amount'].strip()),\n                'bonus': float(row['bonus'].strip()),\n            }\n            timesheet_entries.append(entry)\n    \n    # Find earliest valid date in timesheet\n    valid_dates = []\n    for entry in timesheet_entries:\n        try:\n            d = datetime.strptime(entry['date_str'], '%Y-%m-%d')\n            valid_dates.append(d)\n        except ValueError:\n            # Try to correct: April 31 -> April 30, June 31 -> June 30\n            year, month, day = entry['date_str'].split('-')\n            year, month, day = int(year), int(month), int(day)\n            # Get last day of the month\n            last_day = calendar.monthrange(year, month)[1]\n            if day > last_day:\n                day = last_day\n                try:\n                    d = datetime(year, month, day)\n                    valid_dates.append(d)\n                except:\n                    pass\n            elif month > 12:\n                # Could try to fix month > 12\n                pass\n    \n    if not valid_dates:\n        return {}\n    \n    earliest_date = min(valid_dates)\n    billing_weekday = earliest_date.weekday()  # Monday=0, Sunday=6\n    # If weekday is 1 (Tuesday), then billing_weekday = 1\n    \n    # Determine billing periods\n    # Find all months with records\n    months_with_data = set()\n    for date in valid_dates:\n        months_with_data.add((date.year, date.month))\n    \n    # Generate billing start dates for each month\n    billing_starts = []\n    for year, month in sorted(months_with_data):\n        # Find first occurrence of billing_weekday in this month\n        first_day = datetime(year, month, 1)\n        days_to_add = (billing_weekday - first_day.weekday()) % 7\n        start_date = first_day + timedelta(days=days_to_add)\n        billing_starts.append(start_date)\n    \n    billing_starts.sort()\n    \n    # For each entry, determine billing period\n    # ... process each entry, handle invalid data, etc.\n    \n    # Aggregate\n    employee_monthly = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(lambda: {'hours': 0.0, 'bonus': 0.0}))\n    \n    for entry in timesheet_entries:\n        emp_id = entry['employee_id']\n        # Skip if employee not in our employees list\n        if emp_id not in employees:\n            continue\n        \n        # Parse and validate date\n        try:\n            date = datetime.strptime(entry['date_str'], '%Y-%m-%d')\n        except ValueError:\n            year_s, month_s, day_s = entry['date_str'].split('-')\n            year, month, day = int(year_s), int(month_s), int(day_s)\n            last_day = calendar.monthrange(year, month)[1]\n            if day > last_day:\n                day = last_day\n                try:\n                    date = datetime(year, month, day)\n                except:\n                    continue\n            else:\n                continue\n        \n        # Determine billing period\n        period_idx = None\n        for i, start in enumerate(billing_starts):\n            if date >= start:\n                if i + 1 < len(billing_starts):\n                    if date < billing_starts[i + 1]:\n                        period_idx = i\n                        break\n                else:\n                    period_idx = i\n                    break\n        \n        if period_idx is None:\n            continue\n        \n        # Parse performed tasks - handle errors\n        tasks_str = entry['performed_tasks_str']\n        # Handle malformed task lists\n        if tasks_str == '[]' or tasks_str == '':\n            task_ids = []\n        else:\n            # Clean up: remove brackets if present\n            cleaned = tasks_str.strip()\n            if cleaned.startswith('[') and not cleaned.endswith(']'):\n                cleaned = cleaned + ']'\n            elif cleaned.endswith(']') and not cleaned.startswith('['):\n                cleaned = '[' + cleaned\n            elif not cleaned.startswith('[') and not cleaned.endswith(']'):\n                cleaned = '[' + cleaned + ']'\n            \n            # Parse\n            try:\n                inner = cleaned[1:-1]  # Remove [ and ]\n                if inner.strip():\n                    task_ids = [int(x.strip()) for x in inner.split(',') if x.strip()]\n                else:\n                    task_ids = []\n            except:\n                task_ids = []\n        \n        # For bonus: use the bonus column directly\n        bonus = entry['bonus']\n        if bonus < 0:\n            bonus = 0.0\n        \n        # Aggregate\n        monthly_key = (year, month)  # Use the original month name for grouping, but bill by billing period\n        \n        # Actually use billing period index as key\n        period_key = period_idx\n        \n        employee_monthly[emp_id][period_key]['hours'] += entry['hours_worked']\n        employee_monthly[emp_id][period_key]['bonus'] += bonus\n    \n    # Calculate salary per employee per billing period\n    result = {}\n    for pesel in employees:\n        if pesel in employee_monthly:\n            periods = employee_monthly[pesel]\n            salaries = []\n            for period_idx in sorted(periods.keys()):\n                data = periods[period_idx]\n                total = data['hours'] * employees[pesel]['hourly_rate'] + data['bonus']\n                salaries.append(round(total))\n            if salaries:\n                result[pesel] = salaries\n        else:\n            result[pesel] = []  # Or don't include\n    \n    return result\n```\n\nWait, I need to think about what months to include. The task says \"list of salaries should be sorted by billing month in ascending order.\" If an employee has no records in a billing period, do we include 0 or skip that period?\n\nLooking at the expected format, the list seems to only include months where the employee had earnings.
